text:
maya: quick smoke check — seeing different behavior between JWT service-account auth and OIDC impersonation when a Node client stream reconnects. With JWT the stream resumes fine; with OIDC impersonation we sometimes get a 401 during reconnect and the client never reauths. anyone run into this?

sam: can you paste the minimal repro or logs? sounds like token refresh didn't kick in.

maya: logs: 
```
[2026-02-10T14:22:01.123Z] stream: disconnect, code=1006
[2026-02-10T14:22:01.456Z] auth: using oidc impersonated token, expires_in=300
[2026-02-10T14:22:02.003Z] stream: reconnect -> auth header set
[2026-02-10T14:22:02.210Z] http 401 GET /v1/stream -> invalid_token
[2026-02-10T14:22:02.215Z] client: no reauth attempt scheduled
```
repro steps: node SDK v1.8.2, configured with impersonate=true and target_service_account, short-lived tokens (5m). If I switch to a plain JWT key file flow it reconnects fine.

jared: two quick guesses: (1) audience/aud mismatch for OIDC-issued token on reconnect, (2) SDK's reauth path for impersonation doesn't parse the `expires_in` correctly when reuse happens fast. Can you try ENV `REDWOOD_AUTH_DEBUG=1` and show the auth exchange logs?

maya: toggled REDWOOD_AUTH_DEBUG and saw this on the token refresh path: 
```
fetching token -> url=https://creds.internal/token?impersonate=true
response: {"access_token":"ya29....","expires_in":300}
scheduling refresh at delta=250s
```
but on reconnect the client used the same cached token (which was valid) yet server rejected it.

olivia: fyi i hit a similar-sounding issue last quarter during multi-project impersonation. The bug turned out to be that when the client reused an impersonated token across a region boundary we were accidentally swapping the audience to the default hosted API scope. The fix was to carry the original `target_audience` through the reconnect flow in the SDK.

olivia: can you paste the client init? there was also a bug where passing `projectId` + `impersonate` caused the SDK to build a different aud claim.

maya: client init snippet: 
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  auth: { impersonate: true, target: 'sa@my-org.iam.gserviceaccount.com' },
  region: 'us-west1',
})
client.stream('chat', { ... })
```

sam: try forcing `auth: { impersonate: true, audience: 'https://inference.redwood.ai' }` or explicitly set `target_audience` if your flow supports it. Also check that the impersonation service account has the `iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken` role in the target project.

jared: i've filed a quick smoke issue based on this pattern, linked in the thread: https://git.redwood/infra/issues/3482 — contains repro notes + suggestion to add a reconnect unit test for impersonated tokens.

ci-bot: PR #6127 linked: "node-sdk: carry target_audience through reconnect" (https://git.redwood/sdk/pull/6127) — landed on canary. :white_check_mark:

maya: thanks — i'll try the canary and add explicit audience. if that fixes i'll post minimal repro and mark the issue with steps so eng-runtime can add a test. pinging @devex for visibility. :+1:

sam: if you still see it after canary, share a minimal repro script (5-10 lines) and i'll run it in a few regions. otherwise sounds like olivia's fix is probably it.

maya: will do. thanks everyone!
